name: Asimjeeg Datooga
catalog_citation: Griscom, Richard T. 2019. Topics in Asimjeeg Datooga Verbal Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of Oregon. UO Scholars' Bank, handle 1794/24939.
catalog_locator: Ch. 2, sec. 2.3 'Tone' and 2.3.1 'Underlying tones', pp. 68-69; sec. 2.3.2 p. 70
catalog_quote: This section briefly outlines the tonal system of Asimjeeg Datooga. Tone in Asimjeeg Datooga is a critical component of the grammatical system, and some constructions employ the use of tone as the sole or primary formal coding mechanism ... No thorough analysis of tone in any Datooga variety has ever been completed, although transcriptions of tone are a common feature in the Datooga literature and tone is recognized to play an important role in the grammatical systems of Datooga varieties ... In Asimjeeg Datooga there are two underlying tones: low (L) and high (H). Some minimal pairs exist, such as (37) and (38). The tone-bearing unit (TBU) in Asimjeeg Datooga is the syllable, rather than the mora. This means that syllable shape or weight does not impact the tone-bearing properties of a syllable. Nasals can bear tones in word-initial position only, when they are fully syllabic. ... (37)…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification 'tonal, no word-stress rule stated' rests on the only detailed description of Isimjeega Datooga, a 2019 fieldwork dissertation with a phonetics/phonology chapter, held in full; the deciding quotation is verbatim at the cited sections and pages (2.3 p. 68, 2.3.1 p. 69, 2.3.2 p. 70), and the negative claim (zero 'stress', 'accent' only as diacritic names) is confirmed by a full-text search for stress/accent over the whole text. Glottolog has no descriptive bibliography for this languoid, and API searches (Crossref, Zenodo, ORCID) turned up no later prosody or stress study of this variety; the one open Griscom item on Datooga variation (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.2656438) is a 435 MB video presentation and was not downloaded. Nothing found suggests a stress system that the source missed; Southern Nilotic relatives are likewise described as tonal. no reclassification or re-read is warranted; the two works still to obtain are low
